faq.q: How long does SEO take to actually pay off?
faq.a: Most Ascend clients see measurable ranking and traffic gains within 3–6 months, with revenue impact compounding from month 6 onward. SEO is the only marketing channel where last year's work keeps paying this year — but it punishes shortcuts. We optimize for compounding, not for vanity wins in month one.

faq.q: How is Ascend Growth's SEO approach different from other agencies?
faq.a: Most SEO agencies do SEO. Ascend Growth Partners does PR, content, and SEO as one integrated system — which means our SEO clients get the link authority that pure-SEO agencies can't reach. Our team has run search and PR strategy for clients including Mel Robbins, Ed Mylett, Tim Grover, Gymshark, and BKFC.

faq.q: Do you handle SEO for personal brands and individual founders, or only companies?
faq.a: Both — and personal-brand SEO is one of our specialties. The playbook is different from corporate SEO, and we've run it for some of the biggest personal brands in the world.

faq.q: Can you recover a site that got hit by a Google algorithm update?
faq.a: Yes — algorithm recovery and helpful-content remediation is one of Ascend's core specialties. Whether you're an ecommerce brand running on Klaviyo or a personal brand with a list of 500K, the math is the same: a properly engineered list outperforms every paid channel you have.

chapters.body: A 50,000-person list is not one audience — it's twenty. New subscribers, dormant subscribers, repeat buyers, lapsed VIPs, content-only readers, high-intent browsers. We build segmentation logic, content variants, and send-time strategy so every subscriber gets a message that actually fits where they are. The result is the part nobody talks about: lower unsubscribes, higher inbox placement, and revenue that compounds because subscribers stop tuning you out.

chapters.h2: SMS is a scalpel, not a hammer.
chapters.h2_html: SMS is a scalpel, not a hammer.
chapters.body: SMS open rates clear 95% — which means it works exactly twice before subscribers opt out if you abuse it. We use SMS for the moments that genuinely warrant it: cart recovery, drop launches, time-bound offers, VIP-only access, and high-urgency announcements. Layered correctly with email, SMS adds 15-25% on top of total lifecycle revenue. Deployed badly, it tanks your list health permanently. We do the former.

We've run email programs for some of the largest personal brands in the world, and we know how to scale a creator's list without making it feel transactional. If you're a thought leader, athlete, author, or founder building an audience, your email list is the most valuable thing you own. We treat it that way.

faq.q: What email and SMS platforms does Ascend work with?
faq.a: Ascend works across every major email and SMS platform: Klaviyo, Attentive, Postscript, HubSpot, Mailchimp, ActiveCampaign, Drip, ConvertKit, Beehiiv, and Substack. We'll recommend the right platform for your stack — ecommerce brands usually land on Klaviyo + Attentive, while creators and personal brands often run Beehiiv, ConvertKit, or HubSpot. We manage migrations, setup, and ongoing operations end-to-end.

faq.q: How fast can you build a full email automation system?
faq.a: A complete core automation suite — welcome, abandoned cart, post-purchase, win-back, browse abandonment — typically takes 3–4 weeks from kickoff to live. We prioritize highest-revenue flows first, so you usually see meaningful return inside the first month rather than waiting for the full build to finish.

faq.q: How does Ascend measure email and SMS success?
faq.a: Revenue per send, attributed email and SMS revenue, flow conversion rates, list growth rate, and deliverability health. We don't lead reports with open rates — opens stopped being a reliable metric the moment Apple Mail Privacy Protection launched. Every dashboard ties campaign and flow performance back to actual dollars.

faq.q: Can SMS marketing actually drive meaningful revenue?
faq.a: Yes — SMS regularly delivers 95%+ open rates and click-through rates several multiples higher than email. The catch is that SMS punishes overuse hard: subscribers opt out fast if abused. We deploy SMS surgically — for cart recovery, drops, time-sensitive offers, and VIP segments — which is what unlocks the revenue without burning the list.

faq.q: What if our email list is small, or hasn't been emailed in a long time?
faq.a: Both are normal starting points. For small lists, we build a list-growth strategy alongside the program — popups, lead magnets, partnership flows, paid acquisition where it pencils out. For dormant lists, we run a careful sunset and re-engagement sequence before any major sends so we protect your sender reputation. Sending hard to a cold list is the fastest way to land in spam permanently.

faq.q: Do you work with personal brands and creators, or only ecommerce?
faq.a: Both — and they're completely different playbooks. Ecommerce email is product-driven, transactional, and lives in Klaviyo or HubSpot. Creator email is editorial, audience-driven, and lives in Beehiiv, ConvertKit, or Substack. Ascend has run programs for some of the largest personal brands in the world alongside our ecommerce work, and we don't try to force one playbook onto the other.

faq.q: How does email and SMS fit with the rest of Ascend's services?
faq.a: Email and SMS sit at the bottom of the funnel — they capture and monetize the demand that PR, SEO, social, and paid generate at the top. Ascend clients running our integrated stack typically see email and SMS revenue grow 2–3x faster than clients running standalone programs, because the audiences feeding the list are higher-intent to begin with. The channels compound when they talk to each other.

faq.q: How fast does Google Ads start working?
faq.a: You'll see early signal — clicks, impressions, initial conversions — within the first 1–2 weeks. Stable, optimizable performance typically takes 4–6 weeks of data collection, testing, and bid algorithm learning. Anyone promising "results in 7 days" is either lying or burning your budget on broad match to fake the curve. We'd rather build something that compounds than spike a vanity number in week one.

faq.q: Does Ascend manage Shopping and Performance Max campaigns?
faq.a: Yes — Ascend manages the full Google Ads stack: Search, Shopping, Performance Max, YouTube, Demand Gen, Discovery, and remarketing. Performance Max in particular has become non-negotiable for most ecommerce accounts, but it's also the campaign type most agencies run badly because the asset group structure is unforgiving. We're built for it.

faq.q: Can you fix a Google Ads account that's wasting spend?
faq.a: Yes — and account remediation is one of the most common ways clients start working with us. We audit account structure first, then conversion tracking, then search terms, then bidding strategy, then landing pages, then creative. Most "broken" accounts have 2–3 leaks doing the bulk of the damage, not 30 small ones — finding and patching those quickly is usually where the first ROAS lift comes from.

faq.q: What's the minimum ad spend Ascend works with?
faq.a: Our Google Ads engagements are typically a fit for brands spending $10K/month and up on paid media — that's the spend level where the work we do (server-side tracking, value-based bidding, dedicated optimization cycles) actually pays for itself. Below that, the management fee outweighs the upside, and we'll usually point smaller accounts toward DIY resources or different solutions until they're ready.

faq.q: Do you work with personal brands, course creators, and authors — or only ecommerce?
faq.a: Both, and they're different playbooks. Course launches, book launches, and high-ticket personal-brand offers run on a launch-cycle model with very different bidding strategies than evergreen ecommerce. Ascend has run paid media for some of the largest personal brands in the world alongside our ecommerce clients, and we don't try to force one playbook onto the other.

faq.q: What's the difference between hiring Ascend vs. a typical PPC agency?

Three: we work specifically with founders, personal brands, and challenger companies, so our playbooks are tuned for direct-response and brand-led work — not enterprise lead-gen funnels nobody buys from anyway.

chapters.label: Step 01 — Brand Audit
chapters.h2: Before we pitch a single journalist, we read the room.
chapters.h2_html: Before we pitch a single journalist, we read the room.
chapters.body: Most PR engagements fail in week one — not because of bad pitching, but because no one mapped the story landscape first. We audit your current media footprint, public perception, search results, AI citations, and competitor narrative share. We find the stories already being told about you (the good and the ugly), the stories that should be told, and the open lanes where your brand can own the conversation. That map becomes the entire campaign brief.

chapters.label: Step 02 — Comms Readiness
chapters.h2: Most brands break the moment the press shows up.
chapters.h2_html: Most brands break the moment the press shows up.
chapters.body: Spokespeople who haven't been media-trained. Press kits that don't exist. Messaging that contradicts itself across channels. Founder bios that are three years out of date. We rebuild the communications infrastructure before we go to market — press kits, founder positioning, message hierarchy, response protocols, and crisis playbooks — so when the story lands, your brand is ready to capitalize on it instead of fumble it.

chapters.label: Step 03 — Story & Pitching
chapters.h2: Journalists don't write about products. They write about stories.
chapters.h2_html: Journalists don't write about products. They write about stories.
chapters.body: This is where most PR firms quietly fail — they send press releases pretending to be stories. We engineer actual narrative angles: contrarian takes journalists are itching to publish, data-backed trends with original research behind them, founder origin stories with real stakes, and cultural moments your brand has earned the right to be part of. Then we pitch them through relationships, not blast lists. Our team places clients in Forbes, WSJ, Bloomberg, TechCrunch, Inc., Fast Company, Business Insider, and the verticals that matter for your category.

chapters.label: Step 04 — Engineered Opportunity
chapters.h2: The best PR moments aren't waited for. They're built.
chapters.h2_html: The best PR moments aren't waited for. They're built.
chapters.body: Reactive PR - waiting for press to come find you - is a losing game. We forecast upcoming news cycles, industry inflection points, awards seasons, and cultural conversations where your brand can insert itself credibly. Then we build the moments: original research drops, founder bylines, expert commentary at the right time, partnership announcements, and tied-to-the-news Op-Eds.

faq.q: How long does it take to land Tier 1 media coverage?
faq.a: Most Ascend clients see their first Tier 1 placement within 60–90 days. The first month is spent on brand audit, narrative development, comms readiness, and quietly warming the right journalist relationships — going to market on day one with a half-built story is how PR campaigns die. Once we're pitching, placements compound from there.

faq.q: What counts as a Tier 1 media placement?
faq.a: Tier 1 placements are earned editorial coverage in major national and international outlets: Forbes, The Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg, Reuters, Business Insider, Fast Company, TechCrunch, Inc., and the leading vertical publications in your industry. Sponsored content, paid placements, and contributor pieces in low-authority outlets don't count — and any agency telling you they do is the wrong agency.

faq.q: Does Ascend guarantee placements?
faq.a: No ethical PR firm guarantees specific placements — and any firm that does is either lying or paying for them. What Ascend guarantees is process: a real audit, a real story, the right journalist relationships, the right moments to pitch into, and the persistence to land coverage that actually moves the needle. The proof is the client roster.

faq.q: How is PR different from paid advertising or influencer marketing?
faq.a: Paid ads disappear the moment the budget stops. Earned media is permanent — it gets indexed by Google, cited by ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity, and carries third-party editorial credibility that no ad can replicate. Influencer marketing rents a creator's audience; PR builds your own. The brands that win the long game invest in all three, but PR is the only one that compounds.

faq.q: Can Ascend handle crisis communications?
faq.a: Yes — crisis communications is a core practice at Ascend Growth Partners. We build proactive crisis playbooks for brands before they need them, and we provide rapid-response support when something breaks. The brands we work with — public-facing personalities, combat sports, consumer brands with active social audiences — operate in environments where reputational risk is constant, so we're built for it.

faq.q: Who does Ascend's PR work best for?
faq.a: Ascend works best for founders, personal brands, athletes, authors, challenger companies, and category-defining startups — the people and brands the legacy PR firms move too slowly for. Our roster includes Mel Robbins, Ed Mylett, Tim Grover, Gymshark, BKFC, Toyota, and Keller Williams. We're not the right firm for clients who want the BCG of PR. We're the firm for clients who want the agency that ships.

faq.q: What's the difference between Ascend and a traditional PR agency?
faq.a: Three things. One: speed — we ship in days where legacy firms ship in weeks, partly because the founder built the firm specifically against that constraint. Two: integration — Ascend runs PR alongside SEO, GEO, and AI solutions, so earned coverage compounds across every channel automatically. Three: specialization — we work specifically with founders, personal brands, and challenger companies; we're not trying to also be a Fortune 500 corporate comms firm.

faq.q: Where is Ascend Growth Partners located, and do you work globally?
faq.a: Ascend is headquartered in Toronto and Miami, with a six-person team that works with clients globally. The dual-HQ setup gives us coverage across both Canadian and U.S. media markets, and we regularly run campaigns across U.S., Canadian, and international press for clients in any geography.
